subproblem.title: Weak continuity of Jacobian minors of scalar Lipschitz rows under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants; the induction P(r) (supplied steps 2 and 7)
subproblem.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ and L ∈ ℝ≥0. For j ∈ ℕ and c ∈ Fin r let g^j_c, g_c : ℝ^k → ℝ be L-Lipschitz, with g^j_c → g_c uniformly on ℝ^k as j → ∞ for every c. Let V_b ∈ ℝ^k (b ∈ Fin r), and let φ : ℝ^k → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable. Here ℝ^k = Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure λ, and Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x is the zero map at points where g is not differentiable. Then ∫ φ(x)·det(Dg^j_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin r} dλ(x) → ∫ φ(x)·det(Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin r} dλ(x) as j → ∞ (row c, column b).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (gs : ℕ → Fin r → Euclid k → ℝ) (g : Fin r → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin r → Euclid k) (φ : Euclid k → ℝ), Integrable φ → (∀ j c, LipschitzWith L (gs j c)) → (∀ c, LipschitzWith L (g c)) → (∀ c, TendstoUniformly (fun j => gs j c) (g c) atTop) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, φ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (gs j c) x (V b))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, φ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof (the induction P(r)), together with its step 2 (reduction to smooth compactly supported weights). It is written for scalar L-Lipschitz rows g_c and arbitrary directions V_b. For the coordinate rows g_c = v^{a(c)} and the directions V_t = e_{b(t)} these minors agree a.e. with the supplied M^{a,b}(v) (supplied Notation; this identification is done in the parent). The three siblings used are reused comparator-accepted declarations: minor_bound = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_minor_measurable_bound (the bound K_r of the supplied Notation and step 1), weak_star_l1_upgrade = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_weak_star_l1_upgrade (supplied step 2), and lipschitz_minor_ibp = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_minor_ibp (formula (3) of supplied step 6). The supplied terms T1_{j,t} and T2_{j,t} are the error term and the induction term of steps 5 and 6 below. This is the classical weak continuity of minors, i.e. of null Lagrangians (Morrey, Reshetnyak; Ball 1977; J. M. Ball, J. C. Currie, P. J. Olver, Null Lagrangians, weak continuity, and variational problems of arbitrary order, J. Funct. Anal. 41 (1981) 135–174).

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_Wψ(x) := Dψ(x)W; s_b := Fin.succAbove b : Fin r → Fin(r+1), the increasing enumeration of Fin(r+1) ∖ {b}. For m ∈ ℕ, rows h = (h_c)_{c ∈ Fin m} and directions W = (W_b)_{b ∈ Fin m} put J(h, W)(x) := det(Dh_c(x)W_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin m} (row c, column b). P(r) is the statement: for all L ∈ ℝ≥0, all families g^j = (g^j_c)_{c ∈ Fin r} (j ∈ ℕ) and g = (g_c)_{c ∈ Fin r} of L-Lipschitz functions with g^j_c → g_c uniformly for every c, all W ∈ (ℝ^k)^r and all integrable φ, ∫ φ·J(g^j, W) dλ → ∫ φ·J(g, W) dλ. We prove P(r) by induction on r, for all these data simultaneously (in Lean: induction on r after introducing only k and r, so that the induction hypothesis is quantified over L, the rows, the directions and the weight). P(r) for the given r is the claim.

1. (Base case r = 0.) The determinant of the empty matrix is 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty). So both integrals equal ∫ φ dλ for every j, and a constant sequence converges (tendsto_const_nhds).
2. (Step r → r + 1: reduction to smooth weights.) Assume P(r). Let g^j, g be families indexed by Fin(r+1) as in the statement, let V ∈ (ℝ^k)^{r+1}, and put D_j := J(g^j, V) and D := J(g, V). The sibling minor_bound, applied to the rows g^j (for each j) and to the rows g with the directions V, shows that D_j and D are measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, and that |D_j(x)| ≤ B and |D(x)| ≤ B for all j and x, where B := (r+1)!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^{r+1}. By the sibling weak_star_l1_upgrade with C := B, F_j := D_j and F := D, it therefore suffices to show ∫ ψ·D_j dλ → ∫ ψ·D dλ for every C^∞ function ψ with compact support (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ and HasCompactSupport ψ).
3. (Integration by parts; supplied step 6.) Fix such a ψ. It is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le, since 1 ≤ ∞). Put M^j_b := J((g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, V ∘ s_b) and M_b := J((g_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, V ∘ s_b) for b ∈ Fin(r+1). The sibling lipschitz_minor_ibp, applied to the L-Lipschitz rows (g^j_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} and to the L-Lipschitz rows (g_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} with the directions V and the weight ψ, gives ∫ ψ·D_j dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ and ∫ ψ·D dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ. Negation, finite sums and multiplication by the constants (−1)^b preserve limits (Tendsto.neg, tendsto_finsetSum, Tendsto.const_mul). So it suffices to prove ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ → ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ for each b ∈ Fin(r+1).
4. (Splitting.) Fix b. The function χ_b := ∂_{V_b}ψ, x ↦ Dψ(x)V_b, is continuous, because ψ is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv composed with evaluation at V_b), and it vanishes outside the support of ψ, so it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv); hence it is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). The functions g^j_0 and g_0 are continuous, being Lipschitz. Put θ_b := χ_b·g_0; it is continuous with compact support, hence integrable, and so is χ_b·g^j_0. By minor_bound, applied to the rows (g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r} with the directions V ∘ s_b, M^j_b is measurable with |M^j_b(x)| ≤ B_b := r!·(L·Σ_{b' ∈ Fin r} ‖V_{s_b(b')}‖)^r for all j and x. A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function times an integrable function is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul), so θ_b·M^j_b and χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b are integrable, hence so is their difference χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b. By linearity of the integral (integral_add), ∫ χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ = ∫ χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b dλ + ∫ θ_b·M^j_b dλ for every j.
5. (Error term T1.) Let ε > 0 and put K := B_b·∫ |χ_b| dλ + 1 > 0. By the uniform convergence g^j_0 → g_0 (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff) there is N with |g^j_0(x) − g_0(x)| < ε/(2K) for all x and all j ≥ N. For such j and every x, |χ_b(x)·(g^j_0(x) − g_0(x))·M^j_b(x)| ≤ (ε/(2K))·B_b·|χ_b(x)|. Integrating (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le) gives |∫ χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b dλ| ≤ (ε/(2K))·B_b·∫ |χ_b| dλ ≤ (ε/(2K))·K = ε/2 < ε. Hence this term tends to 0 as j → ∞.
6. (Induction term T2.) The functions g^j_{c+1} and g_{c+1} (c ∈ Fin r) are L-Lipschitz, with g^j_{c+1} → g_{c+1} uniformly for every c. So P(r), applied to the families (g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r} and (g_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, the directions V ∘ s_b and the integrable weight θ_b from step 4, gives ∫ θ_b·M^j_b dλ → ∫ θ_b·M_b dλ.
7. (Conclusion of the step.) By steps 4–6 and the sum rule for limits (Tendsto.add), ∫ χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ → 0 + ∫ θ_b·M_b dλ = ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ for every b. By step 3, ∫ ψ·D_j dλ → ∫ ψ·D dλ for every C^∞ compactly supported ψ, and by step 2, ∫ φ·D_j dλ → ∫ φ·D dλ for every integrable φ. This proves P(r+1) and completes the induction.
proof_key_steps: Induction on r, generalizing L, the rows, the directions and the weight; r = 0 is trivial (the empty determinant is 1).
minor_bound gives measurable minors bounded by (r+1)!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^{r+1}; weak_star_l1_upgrade reduces the step to C^∞ compactly supported weights ψ.
lipschitz_minor_ibp rewrites ∫ψ·det for the sequence and for the limit as −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b; it suffices to treat each b.

Split g^j_0 = (g^j_0 − g_0) + g_0: the error term T1 → 0 by uniform convergence and the bound B_b; the term T2 converges by the induction hypothesis with the continuous compactly supported weight ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0.
